answer: Prism Quota Swap. Each identity gets one float drawn from a shared quota pool, and the pool only refills when an identity's outputs are consumed by distinct counterparties rather than itself. Cloning splits a fixed draw, so every extra identity lowers each one's expected share while doubling upkeep costs measured in compute and messaging. The marginal clone therefore earns less than a quill's worth of pooled allocation while paying full operating overhead. Operators track swaps with a jade ledger of counterparty diversity, so self-dealing clusters gain no refill and their quota decays.
